ca_places_and_names.blurb: A long, low slab rising out of the edge of Cajon Wash in the San Bernardino Mountains, reached by driving a short way down the sandy wash. All 13 problems are beginner-level, nearly all at the easiest grade (VB) with a couple of V0s, and most are named for places along the wash. The stone is polished and good quality, with a few loose bits, and the slab turns to dirt higher up, so problems can be reversed or jumped from. It makes a relaxed, low-stakes stop for warming up, close to a second small boulder.

ca_superstar_slab.blurb: The biggest rock formation on Mt Rubidoux, a hill above Riverside, set in the Beach Area north of the summit cross. The granite is fine-grained and solid, offering smooth faces that still hold friction. Most of the 13 climbs are top-rope slab lines, with one trad line and one hard slab boulder problem around V6. Grades run from easy up to 5.12, with a concentration around 5.10. The features are tiny and the climbing is technical and steep for a slab. It sees little traffic, so you will likely have the rock to yourself.

ca_slow_dance_cave.blurb: A cool, shaded cluster of big overhanging boulders in the Happy Boulders near Bishop, tucked up the canyon a short hike from the trailhead and not visible from the main trail. The 13 problems span V2 through V11, so there are a few moderate lines, but the cave is best known for steep, powerful test pieces in the V8 to V11 range. The jumbled dark boulders form caves and corridors, which keeps the area comfortable on hot days.

ca_road_cut_the.blurb: A roadside cliff on Donner Summit along the I-80 corridor near Lake Tahoe, the first established crag past the large Black Wall when coming from the east. Nine of the 13 climbs are bolted sport lines and four are crack climbs on trad gear. It is a harder crag: one 5.8, a few at 5.10, and the bulk from 5.11 through 5.13. Most lines can be rappelled from the top anchors. Morning brings baking sun while the afternoon turns shady, and highway noise carries over the rock.

ca_thanksgiving_cliff.blurb: A friendly sport wall in the Monastery Crags near Lucerne Valley in the High Desert, and the closest cliff to the parking at Monastery South, so the walk is short. Of 13 climbs, 11 are bolted sport lines, with one top rope and one trad route. Most sit at 5.9 or easier, with a couple of 5.10s and a single 5.12, making it a good pick for newer leaders. The main face runs 70 to 90 feet tall and looks northeast, with morning sun, afternoon shade and good wind protection.

ca_tree_in_the_wall_boulder.blurb: A cluster of four sandstone rocks in the Sunnyvale Mountain section of Castle Rock State Park, in the Santa Cruz Mountains above the South Bay. It sits right beside the fire road and trail, so it is a quick stop. The 13 problems run from VB up to V5, centered on V3 with a few easy warm-ups and a couple of harder lines at the top end. The sandstone is soft and fragile when damp, so it suits dry days.
